cards.title: Henry A. Murray
cards.prompt: The OSS had to choose people for work behind enemy lines and no written test reached what it needed. Who led the assessment program it built instead, what was his civilian field, and roughly how many separate assessments did one candidate face?
cards.body: The Harvard personality psychologist who took the lead on the Office of Strategic Services assessment program. Candidates arrived at Station S under a cover identity they had to hold for three and a half days, and went through 85 to 90 assessments feeding ten rated dimensions. None of it scored knowledge.
cards.answer: Henry A. Murray, a Harvard personality psychologist. A candidate faced 85 to 90 assessments over three and a half days at Station S, under cover, ending in ratings on ten dimensions.

cards.title: The Construction Test
cards.sub: 1943–1945 · Station S, the Willard Estate, Fairfax, Virginia, outside Washington
cards.prompt: In the OSS's individual situational test a candidate was given a building job and two assistants. What exactly was he told to build and in how long, who were the assistants really, and how many candidates in the whole programme finished it?
cards.body: Ten minutes, a glorified tinker-toy, a five-foot cube with seven-foot diagonals, and two "helpers" the candidate could only direct — junior staff who turned steadily lazy, recalcitrant and insulting. Murray and MacKinnon recorded men "markedly upset or enraged by the humiliations they suffered." No candidate ever completed the task.
cards.answer: A five-foot cube with seven-foot diagonals, in ten minutes, with two "helpers" who were junior staff under instruction to obstruct him. None finished — no candidate ever completed the task.

cards.title: "Assessment of OSS Personnel"
cards.prompt: Name the paper where the men who built the OSS assessment programme describe it themselves — journal, volume, year. How many procedures did it list, and how many people did it say went through the assessment centres?
cards.body: Five pages by Murray, who led the programme, and MacKinnon, who directed Station S. It lists 35 procedures, ten rated variables, a scoreboard of red and blue pins for every above- and below-average rating, and the count: about 5,500 men and women through the assessment centres.
cards.answer: Murray & MacKinnon, "Assessment of OSS Personnel," Journal of Consulting Psychology 10(2), 1946, pp. 76–80. Thirty-five procedures; about 5,500 men and women assessed.

cards.title: Why your loop has a simulation round
cards.sub: 1945 onward · Station S to the corporate assessment centre
cards.prompt: The OSS dissolved in 1945 and its candidate records were ordered destroyed. Name the two lines of descent the assessment programme left behind, and say which two features of a modern system design round come straight from the Construction Test.
cards.body: Banks's 1995 study calls the programme "the precursor to both the civilian personnel assessment center movement and to several Special Operations selection programs currently in existence." Station S to the corporate assessment centre to the multi-hour tech loop. The vague brief and the mid-task push are inherited equipment.
cards.answer: The civilian personnel assessment-centre movement, and several Special Operations selection programmes. Inherited: the deliberately vague prompt, and the pressure applied part-way through ("now 100x the users") — because the artifact was never the grade.
